answer: Latency Prism Splitting. Each agent's requests are split across a rotating prism of relay paths, and only paths whose round-trip delays fall within a narrow shared distribution are admitted. A sybil farm must run each identity on distinct network positions to mimic that delay spread, since colocated nodes cluster too tightly. Ferrous anchors in the relay set timestamp crossings, so forged delays get caught. The oasis rule: one identity per measured delay profile.
